subject: Carely PoC MAP — deployment mode & region gating (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@carelyhealth.com>; Tom Weber <tom.weber@carelyhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Carely PoC MAP — initial proposal, evaluation milestones, and region gating

Hi Maya / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. As promised, I pulled together an initial Mutual Action Plan (attached) that maps the evaluation milestones we discussed to deployment-mode decisions (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and the region gating that will unblock your regulatory sign-off. High level summary: 

- Goal: 6-week PoC that validates latency, cost per inference, and data residency controls for the Carely Notes Assistant.
- Options we covered: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (predictable throughput + EU-residency), Private (VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads).
- Your ask (EU data residency + SOC2 evidence + procurement windows) points to Dedicated EU for the PoC as the lowest-risk starting point, while allowing Hosted for non-PHI traffic and burst capacity.

Attachments: Carely_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones), redwood-security-evidence.pdf (SOC2 excerpts and data-retention practices).

Two questions before I lock the schedule: 
1) Do you require fully separated tenant compute (Dedicated) for the PoC, or would a Hosted instance with dedicated EU region and encrypted storage meet legal for the first 6 weeks?
2) What is the legal/procurement target date for NDA/contract signature so we can align the Dedicated capacity reservation?

Proposed quick wins in the MAP: 
- Week 0–1: Contract + SOC2 & data-flow signoff (legal + security questionaire)
- Week 2–3: Dedicated EU cluster provisioned & integration tests (canary traffic)
- Week 4–5: Performance/latency benchmarks vs SLOs and cost report
- Week 6: Acceptance & roll-forward plan (if satisfied: option to convert to Dedicated reserved or Private deployment)

If that sequencing looks reasonable I can schedule the gating call this week and get our Infra team (Karthik/Dylan) to stand up a precise cost estimate for Dedicated EU capacity.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---
References: MAP attached (Carely_MAP_v1.xlsx) and security excerpt.
From: Maya Patel <maya@carelyhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Weber <tom.weber@carelyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Carely PoC MAP — initial proposal, evaluation milestones, and region gating

Hi Irene —

Thanks for this — the MAP looks thorough. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: we must ensure all PHI-classified telemetry and model inputs stay within EU infrastructure for the PoC. That rules out general multi-region Hosted unless there is a guaranteed EU-only tenancy and data-at-rest separation.
- Security: we need the Scoped SOC2 artifacts (more than excerpts) and clear KMS/HSM integration notes for key management. The redwood-security-evidence.pdf is a good start but procurement will ask for the full SOC2 report or a signed AICPA statement.
- Procurement timeline: our Legal/Procurement target is to have contract terms by 24 Aug; procurement team will review vendor terms the week after. If Dedicated capacity requires a lead time >2 weeks for GPU reservation, we need to know soon.

For deployment mode preference: Carely would favor Dedicated in EU for the PoC to avoid back-and-forth on residency. If you can provide a short lead-time plan and cost estimate, we can push procurement to prioritize.

Attaching our procurement worksheet (carely-procurement-questions.xlsx) with the items procurement will require.

Best,
Maya
Director of Product | Carely Health
maya@carelyhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@carelyhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Carely PoC MAP — recommended infrastructure approach and lead times

Irene / team —

Quick internal recommendation based on Carely's constraints: 

1) Start PoC on Dedicated EU pool (3 x A10G-equivalent workers) reserved for 4–6 weeks. That satisfies EU-residency, gives predictable latency, and isolates compute for PHI testing.
2) Offer a Hosted EU fallback for non-PHI traffic and for daytime burst traffic. We'll route non-sensitive calls to Hosted nodes and PHI traffic to the Dedicated pool via request routing rules.
3) Lead times: Dedicated pool provisioning (EU) — 8–10 business days after agreement & payment for the reservation. If Carely can sign within 10 business days we can meet the proposed schedule.
4) Cost estimate: attached cost-estimate-dedicated-eu.xlsx with two sizing options (3-worker conservative and 5-worker performance).

Risk notes: 
- If procurement cannot commit to reservation, we can run a Hosted-only PoC with strict EU tenancy + additional attestations, but performance and isolation won't match Dedicated and may fail your acceptance criteria.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is feasible but has a longer procurement and ops lead time (4–6 weeks). Recommend only if the customer needs an air-gapped environment.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync with Carely procurement to walk through the cost and lead-time.

-Karthik
Head of Infra Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@carelyhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Carely PoC MAP — deployment mode & region gating (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the note and for attaching the procurement worksheet. Based on your residency requirement and procurement timeline, our recommendation aligns with Karthik: plan the PoC on Dedicated EU for PHI traffic with Hosted EU for non-PHI/fallback. Proposed immediate next steps: 

1) Contract & MAP sign-off by 17 Aug (DocuSign link below). If we have signature by 17 Aug, Karthik can provision Dedicated EU cluster the following week to meet your 6-week PoC window.
2) Security gating: we will provide the SOC2 report under NDA; redwood-security-evidence.pdf is preliminary. We can submit the full SOC2 and KMS integration notes via secure drive by 10 Aug.
3) Acceptance criteria (short list): 99th percentile inference latency <= 200ms for 512-token prompts (EU Dedicated), throughput >= 10 req/s sustained, and logs/audits delivered to your retention window.
4) Gated call to align on procurement questions: Thu, 13 Aug @ 11:00 UTC (30 min).

Links: 
- MAP (live): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Carely-MAP-DRAFT
- DocuSign (contract placeholder): https://www.docusign.net/contract/CARELY_MAP_0897

If that timeline works I'll ask Karthik to mark the EU capacity and send a refined cost/commitment table.

Cheers,
Irene
From: Tom Weber <tom.weber@carelyhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Maya Patel <maya@carelyhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@carelyhealth.com; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Carely PoC MAP — deployment mode & region gating (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Irene / team —

We appreciate the clear plan. Procurement had a quick look at the worksheet and wants two items clarified before we sign: 
1) Contract term for the Dedicated reservation (we'd prefer month-to-month for the PoC with a 30-day cancel clause).
2) SLA expectations for the Dedicated pool during the PoC (target uptime %, response times for infra incidents).

I've attached our filled procurement worksheet (carely-procurement-questions.xlsx) and looped in procurement@carelyhealth.com for the formal review. If you can confirm the month-to-month reservation and provide SLA language (even a PoC-level commitment), procurement is comfortable moving to DocuSign this week.

Tom Weber
VP Product Ops | Carely Health
procurement@carelyhealth.com
